newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Pressure builds on Australia dlr as yields decline.
newsitem.headline: Pressure builds on Australia dlr as yields decline.

text.p: The Australian dollar came under renwed pressure at the midsession as an early bounce ran into U.S. and Japanese selling, partly on the AUD/yen cross.

The currency had recovered to US$0.7740 after Asian bids rescued it from a US$0.7695 low, but soon slipped again as the market fretted over its waning yield attraction. Support had been found at US$0.7720 but dealers said the lack of a sustained rally suggested the market was angling for a test of US$0.7680. It was also dragged down on the crosses when the U.S. dollar reacted badly to a widening in the Japanese trade surplus with the U.S. which stirred memories of past trade friction.
By 12.30 pm (0230 GMT) the local dollar was fending off bears at US$0.7729/34 after retreating from an early US$0.7740/45 and US$0.7745/50 late here Wednesday.

Analysts noted the currency was oversold on daily charts after sliding from a US$0.7895 peak on Friday and this was probably not a good time to actively short it. Most preferred to sell into any rally around US$0.7785 with a stop at US$0.7820.
On the downside a break of US$0.7680 would confirm a more lasting downtrend was underway which could even see the dollar plumb the US$0.7550 lows reached in early February.
On the crosses it eased to 97.01/21 yen from 97.55/65 late Wednesday and to 59.8 on its trade weighted index from 60.1.
It followed the U.S. dollar which backed to 124.50/55 yen from an early 125.90/95 after Japan reported its trade surplus with the U.S. rose 11.2 percent in March.

For the local dollar the major handicap remained the prospect of continued contraction in its interest differential over the US$ -- it had actually turned negative for one and two year bonds. Shorter dates could go the same way if U.S. rates were hiked again in May as many expected, while the risk in Australia was for another easing. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
